change.tests/wreck-slice.spec.js: The cross-client trace held ArrowDown for 1250 ms of wall time (page.waitForTimeout). Both clients advance per frame by the frame's real time capped at 0.1 s (src/game-loop.js gameLoop() Math.min(dtReal, 0.1), src/app/game-controller.ts MAX_FRAME_SECONDS), so under load the hold gave the dive too little time and the diver read as stationary. The hold step is now { kind: 'hold', key: 'ArrowDown', frameTimeS: 1.25 }: waitForFrameTime waits for requestAnimationFrame in the page and sums the rAF intervals, capped at 0.1 s as both clients cap them, until they reach 1.25 s, what the old hold gave at 60 Hz. No assertion or threshold changed.
change.tests/reload-resume.spec.js: bootGame dismissed every dialog, including the beforeunload prompt the legacy client arms from maybeSaveDiveState (every SAVE_INTERVAL_MS = 3 s of page time) while diving or in a drill; Chromium shows it after a user gesture, which keyboard.down('s') is. Dismissing it cancels the reload and page.reload() waited out the 30 s test timeout. The handler now accepts beforeunload and still dismisses other dialogs. The two rejection tests pass their corrupted payload to reload(page, save), which writes it again from an init script before the new page's scripts, because the old page's periodic save could overwrite it during the reload. No assertion changed.
change.notAFixedFrameCount: The issue proposed holding for N frames (75 = 1.25 s at 60 Hz). Measured with that version under load (8 workers next to a looping npm run test:unit): the Pixi client ran at 3 to 7 frames per second, so 75 frames held for 10 to 23 s (instrumented run: Pixi holds 10.4 to 22.7 s, frame time 7.1 to 7.4 s; test elapsed up to 56.5 s), and 1 of 10 runs hit the 60 s test timeout in waitForAnimationFrames. Counting capped frame time keeps the same lower bound on the dive's time and took 2.1 to 4.1 s for the Pixi hold under the same load.
